title: The Bureau
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Serialised tradecraft with real pull, but subtitled French across five seasons is genuine friction — subtitles block the half-attention viewing that drives high scores, and the realism is deliberately understated rather than cliffhanger-driven.

title: The Chair Company
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: A conspiracy that escalates weekly gives it a mystery spine, and Robinson's half-hour episodes are short. Cringe comedy is friction for consecutive viewing though — the discomfort is the point, which caps it below a comfort-tier 5.

title: The Day of the Jackal
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 5/5: Assassin-versus-hunter chase structure is one of the most compulsive shapes there is, and every episode ends on a near-miss. Slow Horses (your 5) and Bodyguard (4) are the comps; this is more action-forward than either.

title: The Empress
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 5/5: Lush romantic court drama — the exact register where your scores go top: Bridgerton 5, The Crown 5, The Gilded Age 5. Six-episode German seasons with soap-paced romance and intrigue, which is the easiest possible together watch.

title: The Leftovers
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Emotionally punishing meditation on grief with deliberately withheld answers — Lindelof prioritises ambiguity over resolution. Powerful and cumulative, but individual episodes are draining, so it watches in ones. High sustain, low hook.

title: The Lincoln Lawyer
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Season-long case arcs give it the serialised spine that separates it from the 3★ episodic procedurals, and courtroom beats resolve satisfyingly each week. The Good Wife (your binge 4) is the direct comp — same structure, same score.

title: The Night Of
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Eight-episode closed murder case with a genuine did-he-do-it hook. Deliberately methodical and grim about process rather than thriller-paced, so it sits below the propulsive whodunits at 5 — closest to Adolescence, which you scored 4.

title: The Other Bennet Sister
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 5/5: Austen-adjacent witty period romance — Bridgerton is the tonal comp and you scored it 5. Short BBC run, warm tone, romantic plot engine: the lowest-friction together shape in your data.

title: The Penguin
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Eight-episode gangster rise with betrayals landing at episode ends, so it moves. Grimy, oppressive noir atmosphere caps consecutive viewing — the same bleakness ceiling that holds Ozark and Breaking Bad at 4.

title: The Rehearsal
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Slow-by-design constructed reality where the pleasure is watching an elaborate setup accrete. You scored Jury Duty's warmer, funnier cousin 4 as a rating, but Fielder's colder register plus deliberate cringe makes episodes something you absorb one at a time.

title: The Sopranos
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: The founding prestige-antihero show, built on episodic vignettes and psychotherapy rather than serialised cliffhangers, across six seasons. This is the class where your own scores sit at 3 (Better Call Saul, Veep) — craft over compulsion.

title: The Testaments
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 5/5: Direct sequel to The Handmaid's Tale, which you scored binge 5 with the note 'five star bingeable at the end of seasons'. Same dystopian escape-and-resistance engine, same cliffhanger habit — the strongest possible comp for this axis.

title: The White Lotus
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 5/5: Each season opens with a death and withholds who, so the whole run is a closed mystery with a countdown — extremely strong hook. Self-contained anthology seasons of six to seven episodes avoid the fizzle risk entirely.

title: The Wire
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Famously demands patience — each season builds institutional detail slowly and the first few episodes are deliberately disorienting. The payoff is enormous, which is why it stays at 3 rather than 2: commit to it, don't expect to be pulled through.

title: Unforgotten
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Each series is one cold case across six episodes, so there is a genuine serialised spine and a natural stopping point — not case-of-the-week. Measured British investigative pacing rather than thriller velocity, so 4 not 5.

title: Watchmen
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Nine episodes of dense mythology with real jaw-drop reveals — high sustain in your Dark cluster. Docked one because early episodes are deliberately cryptic, so the hook takes two or three episodes to bite.

title: Wolf Hall
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Austere, candlelit Tudor drama built on whispered political manoeuvring — its own prediction flags the slower register versus The Crown. Short runs help, but the deliberate quiet is the opposite of the soap momentum that scores 5 for you.

title: Your Friends & Neighbors
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 5/5: Heist-of-the-week escalation with a will-he-get-caught spine, played witty rather than bleak — that comedy buffer is what lets it hit 5 where Breaking Bad's grimness caps at 4. Short Apple seasons and Hamm's charm make it effortless.

Binge 4/5: Sheridan cliffhangers and a survival-saga spine drive it forward, with big-star anchoring. Sprawling parallel subplots (the Africa thread especially) stall momentum periodically, so 4 rather than 5.

Binge 5/5: The real-time format makes every episode end mid-crisis — it is the show that arguably invented modern binge structure. Nine seasons is a huge runway and it feels dated, but on hook alone nothing here scores higher.

title: A Murder at the End of the World
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Closed-circle murder at a remote retreat with a fixed suspect list — a strong seven-episode hook. Marling's cerebral, slower register and mild audience heat (Trakt 6.9) keep it off 5.

title: A Spy Among Friends
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 2/5: Literary Cold War espionage told largely through interrogation conversations — its own prediction calls it more Tinker Tailor than Slow Horses, which is precisely the low-momentum end. Talky, elliptical and needing full attention.

title: Alone
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Each season is a genuine attrition arc, which sustains, but the meditative pace and absence of manufactured drama mean no cliffhanger pull — its own prediction flags exactly this against Survivor. Comfortable steady viewing.

title: Am I Being Unreasonable?
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Six short episodes with a mystery/thriller backbone building to a real twist — short plus a withheld secret is a strong hook. A prickly, uncomfortable lead adds friction, so 4 rather than 5.

title: Annika
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Case-of-the-week marine homicide with only a light serial thread — the low-hook shape, and its own stated comp is Elsbeth at 3★. Pleasant and light with a distinctive narration gimmick, but nothing pulls to the next episode.

title: Apple Cider Vinegar
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Six-episode fraud unravelling with a cultural-moment engine — the propulsive true-crime shape that works for you (The Dropout, Quiz). Unlikeable subject and a smug narrative register add friction, so 4 not 5.

title: Atlanta
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Loosely connected surreal vignettes with standalone bottle episodes and little forward plot — deliberately anti-serial. Short episodes make it easy, but the experimental structure gives no momentum.

title: Bait
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Conspiracy thriller that escalates from an audition into an existential chase, so it has a real spine, and it is a short complete run. Trippy, disorienting execution and mild audience heat (Trakt 6.5) cap it at 4.

title: Blue Lights
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Its own prediction stresses it is character-driven rather than case-of-week filler — six-episode Belfast seasons with serialised threat arcs and real tension. Grim, high-stress register keeps it below 5.

title: BoJack Horseman
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Short episodes and a serialised depression arc help, but the show gets progressively heavier and the no-franchise-hook problem is a real engagement barrier for you specifically — your animated wins are all IP-driven.

title: Bookish
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Cosy post-war case-of-the-week mystery — the low-hook structure, and IMDB 6.8 suggests execution lags the premise. Light and easy but with no serial pull; closest to Annika and Elsbeth at this level.

title: Catherine the Great
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Only four episodes, so low commitment, but reception is soft (TMDB 6.7) and it plays as a stately costume portrait rather than a plotted drama. Handsome and slow — steady rather than compelling.

title: Chad Powers
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Broad half-hour sports comedy with a disguise premise that generates episodic near-misses, plus an underdog arc. Easy low-friction viewing in the Superstore lane; a slight one-joke risk keeps it off 5.

title: Chief of War
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Handsome historical epic, but largely subtitled Hawaiian with dense unfamiliar political context, and battle-campaign pacing rather than a mystery hook. Requires full attention, which suppresses momentum.

title: Deadwood
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Dense Shakespearean dialogue that demands close listening, and plotting driven by town politics rather than cliffhangers. Rewarding but effortful — the prestige-heavy class where your scores sit at 3.

title: Dear Mama
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Five-part documentary with a strong dual-portrait structure and archival momentum, but documentary format lacks narrative cliffhangers and you have almost no comps in this territory, so calibration is cautious.

title: Detectorists
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Deliberately becalmed gentle comedy where very little happens — its own prediction says it is the antithesis of momentum-driven TV. Half-hour episodes make it frictionless, but there is no pull whatsoever, only warmth.

title: Dexter: Resurrection
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Serial-killer case engine plus a season-long pursuit arc is propulsive, and Trakt heat is high. Held at 4 by revival-fatigue risk and the fact that your serial-killer adjacents underperformed on engagement (Mindhunter, Killing Eve).

title: DTF St. Louis
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Seven-episode non-linear crime story where the structure withholds how the death happened — a reveal engine, which is your strongest hook type. Conrad's discursive style and mid audience heat (Trakt 7.4) cap it.

title: Eric
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: A missing-child hook should drive hard, but execution splits attention across grief, addiction and an imaginary puppet, diluting the search. Bleak 1980s register makes consecutive episodes heavy going.

title: Good American Family
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Built on a perspective-flip — each episode re-tells events from another side, which is a strong structural hook — over a short complete run. Distressing subject matter and an unreliable-narrator device that frustrates some viewers keep it at 4.

title: Hijack
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 5/5: Real-time single-incident thriller — the 24 structure, where every episode ends mid-crisis. Seven episodes with Elba anchoring makes it the easiest kind of together watch, even though S2 reportedly dips in quality.

title: HIS & HERS
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 5/5: Duelling-suspects murder mystery where each spouse suspects the other — a closed question with a built-in twist, over a short complete run. Broadchurch (5) and Matlock (5) are the together comps for exactly this engine.

title: His Dark Materials
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Quest narrative with cliffhanger episode endings across three tight complete seasons — real forward drive. Held at 4 because the fantasy has no psychological-sci-fi hook, which its own prediction flags as your engagement risk.

title: Interview with the Vampire
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Framed as an interrogation of an unreliable narrator, so it withholds and reveals steadily — a decent hook, with lush melodrama helping. Style-over-substance risk and a talky register keep it off 5.
